headline: Your partner got a promotion. Dinner is on them.
An old friend drops by unannounced. You talk until 3am.
A delighted client slips you a thank-you bonus you did not invoice for.
Your kid's first word was "deploy". You are not sure how to feel.
Your gym buddy drags you through a four-week streak.
You caught a cold. There are tissues in the keyboard.
Your landlord "regretfully" raises the rent. Again.
Your partner points out you have said "one sec" for six hours.
A sleepless week with the newborn. Coffee is a food group now.
A friend's wedding weekend: open bar, bad dancing, good speeches.
Family emergency. You drop everything and catch the next flight.
Parked for "just five minutes". The city disagreed.
The sushi place was not, in fact, "probably fine".
A joke about your company does numbers. Your DMs are a warzone.
Your friends throw you a surprise party. You genuinely did not see it coming.
A tax refund lands. Past-you filed something right for once.
Your upstairs neighbour takes up the drums. At night.
Your partner asks you to take one weekend off. Just one.
body: They have not asked for anything in a while, which is its own kind of asking. The sprint ends Sunday either way.

headline: Your mother needs someone to drive her to appointments for a month.
body: Your sibling cannot. She has not asked directly, which is how you know.

headline: A friend's startup wants you as an advisor, for equity in something unproven.
body: They want the name as much as the hours, and they are honest about that. The equity is worth nothing today and might stay that way.

choices.label: Say yes to two hours a month
Skip the advising and write a small cheque
Tell them you have nothing left this year
choices.detail: Free · relationships −4 · mood +2 for the honesty

headline: Your best friend's wedding lands on launch week.
body: The date was set eleven months ago. The launch date was set by you, last Tuesday.

effects.reason: A wedding you promised to attend

choices.label: Send a gift and your apologies

headline: Your kid's recital is at the same hour as a dinner you were told to attend.
body: She has practised the same eight bars every evening for a month. The dinner is the kind you get asked to once.

choices.label: Sit in the third row with a phone that stays in your pocket

headline: Your doctor uses the word "concerning" about your bloodwork.
body: Nothing urgent. Nothing to ignore either. She writes down three things and asks you to actually do them.

headline: Your landlord is selling. You have sixty days.
body: The letter is polite and final. Sixty days is plenty if you start this week and not nearly enough if you don't.

choices.label: Ask three friends and buy pizza
Pay movers and get it over with

headline: Your brother asks to borrow money and will not say what for.
body: He asked by text, at eleven at night, with the amount in it. He has never asked before.

headline: Your partner has an offer in another city and is waiting to see your face.
body: It is the job they talked about long before they met you. They have not said what they want you to say.

choices.label: Tell them to take it and work out the rest
Ask them to stay one more year

headline: The school has changed pickup to 3pm and nobody asked the parents.
body: Three o'clock is the middle of the afternoon and the middle of everything. The other parents already have a rota spreadsheet.

headline: A school reunion invitation arrives, addressed to who you used to be.
body: There is a form asking what you have been up to. You start typing and delete it four times.

choices.label: Go and answer "so what do you do" forty times

headline: A founder friend calls at midnight and does not really want advice.
body: He is talking fast about nothing in particular, which is how he does this. You have both been here before, on different ends of the phone.

headline: Your car makes the noise and then stops making any noise at all.
body: The mechanic says “at this mileage” twice, in the tone that means it. The bus goes near enough, most days.

choices.label: Sell it and take the bus

headline: Someone who loves you suggests, carefully, that you talk to somebody.
body: They have clearly been working up to saying it for a while. They also have a name and a number written down already.

headline: There is a dog at the shelter that has decided you are its person.
body: She came to the front of the pen and stayed there. The volunteer mentions, lightly, that nobody has asked about her in six weeks.

choices.label: Walk away, think about it for a year

headline: You look at your personal account and it is smaller than the company's.
body: You have been paying yourself the minimum for long enough that it stopped feeling like a decision you were making.

headline: Your family does Sunday lunch and has stopped expecting you.
body: Nobody has said anything about it, which is worse. They set the table for the number of people who usually come.

headline: Your ceiling develops an opinion about the flat upstairs.
You find the guitar behind the door. It needs new strings and forty minutes.
You have slept less than five hours for nine days and it shows in the standup.
Your partner cooked the thing you liked when you were both broke.
There is a drawing on the fridge of you, at a desk, with a laptop.
It was your birthday yesterday and you found out from a bank email.
Your neighbours invite you over and you cannot remember their names.
body: You have lived next to them for two years and exchanged nods. The invitation is handwritten and pushed under the door.

choices.label: Go, bring wine, learn the names

headline: You have been asked to give a speech and given three weeks' notice.
body: You were asked because you are the one who is good at talking to rooms. Three weeks is plenty, and three weeks vanishes.

headline: You are awake at 4am doing arithmetic about runway.
A great-aunt you met twice has left you something.
You sign up for a 10k in a moment of optimism.
body: It is eight weeks out and you were feeling good about yourself at the time. The entry fee has already left your account.

choices.label: Actually train for it
choices.detail: Health +16 · energy −4 · eight weeks of mornings

headline: Your partner has an idea and wants to know if it is any good.
body: It is not a good idea. They are not asking you as a founder.

choices.label: Ask questions instead of giving verdicts
Tell them what is wrong with it

headline: They are digging up your road for eight weeks.
Someone lists you as a reference without asking.
body: The call comes in cold, from a recruiter who assumes you are pleased to help. You remember exactly how they worked.

choices.label: Give them a glowing one anyway

headline: You are single, it is a holiday, and everyone else has plans.
body: The office is empty, the flat is quiet, and the group chat is full of other people's photographs.

choices.label: Text six people and see who answers

headline: Someone interesting matches with you and asks a real question.
body: They asked something you actually want to answer. You have been leaving messages four days out of habit rather than strategy.

headline: Your kid is up all night with a fever and the meeting is at nine.
body: By four in the morning it is a bad night rather than an emergency. The meeting was booked three weeks ago and cannot easily move twice.

choices.label: Go in on two hours of sleep

headline: The friend you get lunch with every month is moving abroad.
An estate agent sends you a listing you would have laughed at three years ago.
Your flight credit from a cancelled holiday expires in a month.
body: It is enough for five days somewhere warm, and it disappears at the end of the month whatever you do.

choices.label: Book five days somewhere with bad wifi

headline: The drummer upstairs moves out. The silence is startling.
Someone emails about code you wrote eight years ago that still runs somewhere.
The gym emails to say they miss you. You have paid them for fourteen months.
body: The email says they miss you and includes a graph of your visits. There is one bar on it, in March.

headline: Your partner asks where this is going, and means the company as much as the two of you.
body: It is not a fight. They ask it calmly, at the kitchen table, and then wait for as long as it takes.

choices.label: Give them a real answer with a date in it
choices.detail: Relationships +16 · you have to keep it

choices.label: Say it depends on the next launch

headline: Your anniversary with {partner} is this week.
body: They booked the table a month ago and have not mentioned it since, which is how you know it matters. The week is what it is.

choices.label: Take the wavering hire out instead
choices.detail: An evening · bond +10 with your unhappiest hire · affection −20

headline: Your anniversary again. You missed the last one too.
body: {partner} hasn't brought it up. That is not the same as not noticing. There is no table booked this year.

choices.label: Be there — all of it
choices.detail: An evening · affection +22 · the last miss is forgiven

choices.label: Flowers, again
choices.detail: Affection −25 · they don't say it's fine

headline: {partner} brings up the evening you didn't come to.
body: Not angrily, which is what makes it land. They ask, over the washing up, what it would take for the next one to be different.

choices.label: Take them somewhere this week
choices.detail: An evening · affection +18 · −$300 · the miss is forgiven

headline: {child}'s birthday is on Saturday.
body: They asked whether you'd be there, in the way kids ask when they already know the answer. The party is at four. The week is launch week, or it might as well be.

choices.label: Take the afternoon for the party
Send a present with a card you didn't write

headline: {child}'s birthday. You missed the last one too.
body: They didn't ask this year. There is a drawing on the fridge of everyone who was there last time; you are not in it.

choices.label: Be there, early, and stay to the end
choices.detail: An evening · relationships +16 · mood +12 · the last miss is forgiven

headline: {child} asks why you weren't at the party.
body: It comes out at bedtime, the way the real questions do. Not a complaint — a question, which is worse.

choices.label: Take a day, just the two of you
choices.detail: An evening · relationships +14 · mood +10 · the miss is forgiven

choices.label: Explain what a launch is to a six-year-old

headline: The date you gave {partner} is this week.
body: You said a date. They wrote it down. It is on the fridge, under the magnet from the launch party, and the week has arrived.

choices.label: You shipped. Take the week you promised.

headline: {partner} has stopped asking where this is going.
body: They don't mention the date any more. They have started making plans that don't have you in them, and telling you about them afterwards.

choices.label: Cancel the week and go away together

headline: The year you asked {partner} for is up.
body: They didn't set a reminder. They didn't need to. The job is still there, and so is the question, and this time they are not waiting to see your face.

choices.label: Tell them to take it — you'll make it work from here
choices.detail: Affection +20 · relationships +18 · energy −12 for the commuting

headline: {child} has stopped practising.
body: The eight bars were for you. They say they are bored of the piano now, in the voice that means something else.

choices.label: Ask them to play it for you tonight
Say you'll hear it at the weekend

headline: The fever hasn't broken. Second night.
body: The meeting went fine. Nobody at the meeting is awake at three in the morning holding a thermometer.

choices.label: Go in again
choices.detail: Energy −18 · health −6 · relationships −10 · you catch it

headline: The weekend you said you'd take after the launch.
body: The launch happened, or it didn't. Either way it is eight weeks later, and {partner} has kept count.

headline: {child} said a whole sentence today, and it was about work.
body: “Daddy is on a call” — or the local equivalent. It came out complete, in order, and slightly weary, which is the part that lands.

choices.label: Stop, write it in the notebook, stay on the floor an hour

headline: {child} starts school on Monday.
body: The uniform is too big on purpose. Drop-off is at nine, which is the hour the week gets decided in.

choices.label: Walk them in, both of you pretending not to be nervous
Let someone else take them and ask about it that evening

headline: {child}'s door has been closed for three days.
body: Not slammed. Just closed, in the way that means the house is now two houses. Kids grow up faster than companies, and this one got there first.

choices.label: Knock, sit on the floor of the hallway, wait them out
Give them space — and take the evening back

headline: {child} found a flat.
body: Two buses away, a deposit you offered to cover and they refused. The van is booked for Saturday morning.

choices.label: Drive the van yourself, carry the heavy end
Send money and a good-luck message
